Subject: SIG: Event logging, retention, and customer log access for FinTrack

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks for the quick intro call today. As part of our procurement/compliance review we need some SIG-level confirmations and a small set of evidentiary artifacts related to event logging. Our security team asked for the following by EOD Wednesday (2/17) if possible: 

1) A short description of event types Redwood logs (auth events, model inference requests, admin changes, platform errors, etc.) and where those are captured.
2) Current retention periods for tenant-level audit logs and whether customers can extend/shorten retention.
3) The mechanism for customer access to their logs (self-serve? export on request? S3 access?).
4) Any redaction/pseudonymization practices applied before logs are made available.
5) A sample CSV (redacted) showing the common fields we would see.

Also we prefer a one-page SIG response we can attach to our vendor review and a short runbook for on-demand exports. Can you confirm ownership and timeline?

Thanks,
Laura Chen

Hi Evelyn / Laura / Markus,

Thanks — happy to own the SIG responses. Below are concise answers formatted for your questionnaire. I've attached a one-page SIG response (sig_response_20260216.pdf) and a redacted CSV sample (event_log_sample_20260216.csv). Markus and I sync'd on the export workflow and I'll inline that too.

1) Event types and capture locations- Authentication: successful/failed logins, MFA challenges — captured in identity service logs (tenant-scoped)
- Authorization/Admin changes: role changes, API key creation/revocation — captured in control-plane audit logs
- Inference events: model request metadata (request id, model variant id, token counts, latency) — captured in inference event stream (separate non-PII stream)
- System errors/alerts: infra-level metrics and exception traces — captured in observability pipeline (retained for internal ops)

2) Retention- Default tenant-level audit logs: 90 days (configurable for enterprise customers)
- Inference event stream (detailed telemetry): 30 days by default; aggregated metrics retained longer for platform analytics
- Extended retention: enterprise tier customers can request retention extensions up to 365 days via a contract amendment (subject to storage and compliance review)

3) Customer access to logs- Self-service: Customers can request on-demand exports via the Redwood Console -> Support -> Log Exports. Exports generate tenant-scoped CSV/JSON bundles and are delivered to a customer-owned S3 bucket (preferred) or via a one-time signed URL.
- Access model: we do not provide direct cross-account read access to our internal buckets; exports are push-model (we push to customer bucket) or transient signed download.
- Audit trail: every export request is recorded in the control-plane audit log and a ticket is generated for traceability.

4) Redaction & Pseudonymization- We never surface raw PII in exported logs. Fields that may contain identifiers (user_id, session_id) are hashed with a tenant-scoped salt for exported artifacts unless the customer requests otherwise and has an approved data processing agreement.
- Sensitive fields (credit_card_summary, full_text_input when in high-sensitivity mode) are redacted from exports by default.

5) Sample attached- See event_log_sample_20260216.csv (redacted tenant ids, no PII). Columns: timestamp, tenant_id_hash, event_type, request_id, model_id, tokens_in, tokens_out, latency_ms, outcome

Export runbook summary (from infra):
- Request path: Console export or Support portal -> choose time range -> select format (CSV/JSON) -> choose delivery (customer S3 OR signed URL)
- SLA: standard ad-hoc exports are processed within 24 hours; priority exports (contracted) within 4 hours.
- Costing: small exports (<10GB) included for enterprise customers; larger or frequent bulk exports evaluated and priced (storage + egress).
- Security: exports are delivered encrypted (TLS to signed URL or Server-side-encrypted to customer S3).

Attachments: sig_response_20260216.pdf (formatted SIG answers), event_log_sample_20260216.csv (redacted sample), export_runbook_20260217.md (detailed steps).

Let me know if you need a short attestation line for the SIG or additional evidence (screenshot of export UI, or a short screencast).

Best,
Monica Patel
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
